newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM favours Chidambaram's budget - speaker.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM favours Chidambaram's budget - speaker.

text.p: The speaker of India's lower house, P.A. Sangma, said on Monday that Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral had indicated he supported the government budget presented in February by former finance minister P. Chidambaram.

Sangma told reporters after a meeting with Gujral that the new prime minister wanted to push a budget covering the entire 1997/98 (April-March) fiscal year through parliament. "His (Gujral's) indication is he will go by the old budget," Sangma said, referring to Chidambaram's plan.

Chidambaram's budget, which sparked a rally in share prices after it was introduced in February, has been held hostage to a political crisis which resulted in the downfall of former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

Gujral, who was sworn in on Monday, has not publicly stated whether his centre-left government would back Chidambaram's tax-cutting budget or propose a new plan. Sangma confirmed that parliament would not take up the budget before April 30.

Sangma said parliamentary officials were examining whether Gujral would have to re-introduce a budget or could simply leave Chidambaram's before parliament. "It is a procedural aspect which we have never faced earlier," he said.
The house speaker said the government hoped that the lower house would approve the Finance Bill, which incorporates tax and tariff measures, by May 11 so that the president could sign it by May 14.
